## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the 42 charge documents was traced to a source atom (rule sentence, ladder tier, parameter, measure, eligibility evidence contract, lifecycle transition or tool contract). Sentences that go beyond a literal rule sentence are derivations the source fixes:
- protest_documentation_share note 2 / wage_record_relief_share "fewer than twelve whole months ... 11 October counts, 10 October does not" — the `within_months` primitive (`0 <= MONTHS(filed, NOW) < 12`).
- interest_months "A whole month is completed each time the calendar reaches the due date's day of the month again"; "most recently entered" bill; "most recent" payment — `MONTHS`, `XLATEST(... date_field='entry_date')`.
- monthly_protest_interest "so it arises only where an amount has been billed for that quarter" — compute guard `billed_for_quarter > 0` (see **P2**: the rule text itself does not state the guard).
- credits_on_charges rule 2 "judged from the Department's ledger record", relief_by_appeal "read from the Department's appeal record", one_position_per_claim "never from the caller's account" — evidence_contract authority `system_record`.
- answer_window/relief/notice docs "Day one is the day after the mailing date" — `counting_rule`.

Additions / rewrites / omissions: none found. No "confirm with the customer", "review again", "notify after", or fallback procedure appears.

Prerequisite-side specific checks:
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …", the other problem's tool name in the blocked problem's documents, the resolving action beside the state-form sentence): **none**. protest_decisions names only `grant_charge_protest_0f56e95e`; `file_charge_protest_73ec7ae2` occurs only in protest_filing (scoped grep of tool names over docs/charge).
- A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact: **none**. No document contains this task's figures, names or states (scoped grep for 274.88, 272.16, 3,908.10, 4,286.10, 3,567.90, Marisol, Saint Odile: no hits). answer_abatement Case 1 ("The notice of claim was never answered; the employer's submissions on the position show only a protest") is a labelled hypothetical tier case, not a world fact.

### Source-side problems found (reported, not re-judged against the documents)
- **P1 — retired clause still encoded by an un-retired parameter (policy side; affects both tasks' relief-credit policies).** Both `charge_ext_protest_relief_credit.overwrite[2]` and `charge_ext_response_relief_credit.overwrite[2]` retire the base clause "otherwise payments issued before the late response stay charged even if relief is later granted". The same semantics remain live in the source as variant parameter `relief_bar_for_payments_before_late_response: true` in all seven variants, bound in `charge_evt_notice_and_response.params` and described in `parameter_schema` as "Whether payments issued before a late response stay charged even if relief is later granted". The KB carries both source atoms faithfully, so the corpus now contradicts itself: notice_and_response_af685a20 says the clause "is **no longer in force** ... and it is not applied", while notice_response_terms_8657c3d9 — "The terms below govern the notice of claim and the employer's separation and wage response" — lists "Payments issued before a late response stay charged even if relief is later granted | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes". Nature: an undeclared conflict on the policy side (the overwrite retires the clause but not the parameter that encodes it). Per Step 4 the documents are not re-judged on this basis. No scored value moves in this task (no separation response on record, so neither reading applies), but the contradiction is visible and would bear on any task whose employer answered late without good cause.
- **P2 — rule text vs compute, monthly protest interest (charge_ext_protest_amount).** Rule: "when the employer's tax account shows interest assessed for the statement's quarter, the latest month of that assessed interest in proportion to the protested principal over the amount billed for the quarter". Compute: `(interest_assessed_latest * protested_principal / billed_for_quarter) if (interest_assessed_latest > 0 and billed_for_quarter > 0) else (...)`. With interest assessed but nothing billed (e.g. a contributory employer with interest on late contributions for the statement quarter) the rule is undefined (division by zero) and the compute yields 0. The KB follows the compute ("so it arises only where an amount has been billed for that quarter"). No scored value moves here (billed 3,908.10).
- **P3 — rule text vs compute, interest months (charge_ext_protest_amount, minor).** Rule speaks of "the reimbursement bill ... was paid after its due date"; compute takes `bill_paid_on` = the latest `taxacct_payment_received` entry for the quarter of any component, and compares only that latest date with the due date. A part payment before the due date followed by a later penalty/interest payment would be read as "paid after its due date". The KB follows the compute ("the payment received and applied to that quarter ...; where several are recorded, the most recent one"). No scored value moves (single payment 2026-11-19).
- **P4 — referent of a retained base clause (minor).** charge_evt_credits keeps "an appeal decision relieving the employer credits as a relief does" while the relief clause it points to is retired; the KB (credits_on_charges rule 3, table "Appeal reversal | As a relief credits") carries it as the source has it. Not relevant to this task.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS** for the documents. Every normative atom of charge_ext_protest_amount and charge_ext_protest_relief_credit (rules, baselines with their default constants, all ten factor ladders with every tier, thresholds in figures, windows, rounding moments and order, the prerequisite sentence, both tool contracts) and of the base policies they reference has an equivalent home; the three retired clauses are written as retired in their bearing documents and their unnamed sibling clauses stay in force; no document adds or retires anything on its own. Source-side problems P1–P4 are recorded above with their nature; P1 is a visible contradiction the policy side must resolve (it originates in the un-retired parameter, not in the rendering). First revision; no earlier revision exists.
